title: Charts attached to briefings; Airvan cruise settings; fuel checks linked to the nav log
notes: Browse NAIPS charts: tap Attach on a chart (GAF, GPWT, SIGWX, PCA) and it is fetched with every briefing and shown with it; attached charts are listed beside the Charts row.
GA8 fuel plan: every AFM cruise setting selectable – 2,500 RPM (about 75 %), 2,400, 2,300 (about 65 %) and 2,000 RPM long range.
Fuel checks and the nav log are one set of data: a check at a waypoint fills its row, a logged FOB creates the check.
Load winds (forecast model) for per-leg winds without NAIPS; NAIPS charts fetched by key with GAF and GPWT included.

title: Times in UTC; briefing validity; en route alternates list; chart browser
notes: All clock times are now UTC by default: ETD, Now buttons, nav log, fuel checks, plan import and logbook exports. Status › Pilot can switch to device local time. Records carry their convention; the Enroute page warns when an entered time is hours off the plan.
Briefing requested for a period covering the arrival plus a day, so NOTAMs starting later today or tomorrow are included.
En route alternates are added one code at a time as a list; the chart browser lists NAIPS charts on opening; a Copy wind diagnostics button appears when winds fail.

Load winds (forecast model): per-leg winds and temperatures from the Open-Meteo model at the cruise pressure level, needing no NAIPS route; NAIPS charts fetched by key with GAF and GPWT included; optional NAIPS stored route code for the NAIPS wind profile.

title: Alternates and minima: take-off alternate, approach DA/MDA, en route alternates; NAIPS charts; W&B fuel in volume and weight
notes: Plan: Destination alternate 1 and 2 plus Enroute alternates (as required); a Minima for this flight table with an editor per aerodrome for alternate planning minima, take-off alternate minima and each approach's DA/MDA and visibility.

Briefing rules: approach minima compared with the forecast at ETA (supports all, some or none of the approaches; none at the destination means an alternate), INTER/TEMPO below approach minima flagged, take-off alternate requirement from the departure's current weather, en route alternates assessed for a mid-flight diversion.
Area charts (NAIPS): the Planning Chart Australia, GAF, GPWT and SIGWX charts from the NAIPS chart directory, viewed in the Plan page.
W&B fuel rows show a volume box (L or US gal) beside a weight box; either can be typed.
Plan import accepts OzRunways .ozpln files (airways, LSALTs, winds, level, ETD).

title: Plan import from EFBs, aerodrome minima table, tidier Plan page, NAIPS corrections
notes: Import a plan from OzRunways (.ozpln, with airways, LSALTs, winds, level and ETD), AvPlan, ForeFlight or Garmin (FPL), or a GPX route; the file's waypoints are kept with the plan so they resolve without a navigation database. Paste route for a typed route.
Aerodrome minima table (Status › Navigation data): alternate minima per aerodrome from your documents, CSV import or the fleet pack; used by the briefing rules in place of the defaults.
Plan page in collapsible sections with the action buttons and briefing always visible; briefing header shows the minima applied in words.

NAIPS: winds now come from an SPFIB with expanded winds; briefing decoding follows NAIPS's real layout (NAME (ICAO) headers, two-digit NOTAM numbers, wrapped reports), so NOTAMs for smaller aerodromes are no longer lost and METARs keep their header; a debug view shows the last request and reply.
openAIP navaids and reporting points can be loaded into the navigation data.

title: Navigation log; NAIPS client corrected against the live service
notes: Enroute page: a navigation log with every waypoint of the route, planned ETA and fuel on board from the fuel plan, actual time (tap now) and fuel entries, revised ETAs from the last actual time, fuel difference from plan and a projected fuel at destination with a reserve warning. Included in the flight record and PDF.

NAIPS: the login check now uses an operation NAIPS actually provides (there is no authenticate operation); briefing requests carry one alternate; flight plan filing follows the published schema for supplementary information, SARTIME, PBN and lat/long waypoints. Confirmed against the live service: login and a location briefing from the installed app.

title: Radar, airspace, IFR routes and custom charts on the plan map
notes: Rain radar overlay (Bureau of Meteorology composite via RainViewer) with a two-hour animation on the plan and enroute maps; the enroute page now has a read-only map.

Prohibited, restricted and danger areas: load them under Status › Navigation data from the Airservices Airspace Data CSV, openAIP (with your key) or GeoJSON; the planner lists every area the track crosses with limits and the planned level against them, warns, draws them on the map and keeps the result in the pre-flight record.

IFR routes: import the Airservices General Aviation Data CSV files (waypoints, navaids, routes with LSALT) and type routes with airway designators; the planner expands them, shows LSALT per leg, warns when the level is below it, files airways as ATS route segments and draws routes and waypoints on the map for tapping.
Route suggestions from the routes you have used before for a city pair and from the operator connector (GET /routes).
Custom chart sources (tiles or WMS) for licensed charts, as base maps or overlays, settable by the operator's fleet pack.

title: NAIPS direct from the installed app
notes: The installed iOS/Android app now talks to NAIPS directly with your own NAIPS login: briefings, winds and flight plan filing with no connector or server. The connector's NAIPS client, weather and NOTAM decoding, briefing rules and fuel requirement are bundled into the app (data/naips-lib.js) so both give the same answers.

Status › Operator link gains a NAIPS access setting (Automatic, Direct, Always through the connector) and says whether this copy is the installed app or a browser. In a browser a connector is still required, because Airservices does not accept NAIPS requests from web pages.
The Plan page states which NAIPS path is in use; Test connection without a connector reports NAIPS direct and what it provides.

title: Interactive plan map, equipment code pickers, running your own connector
notes: Plan map: Street, Terrain and Satellite hybrid base layers, an optional openAIP aeronautical overlay (airspace, aerodromes, navaids) with a free key, aerodromes you can tap to set departure, destination, via or alternate, legs you can tap to insert a turning point, and via points you can remove. Turning points are written as ICAO lat/long in the route and the flight plan.
Equipment (10a), Surveillance (10b) and PBN now have Choose… pickers listing every ICAO code with its meaning, and a warning line for mismatched codes.

NAIPS login: the app now explains that NAIPS can only be reached through a connector and points to connector/README.md, which gains a Run your own section (free Render deployment, Dockerfile) so a pilot can use a personal NAIPS login without an operator.

title: POH fuel planning, winds, personal NAIPS login, full EFB file
notes: Fuel plan from the POH: the Plan tab now builds the fuel plan by segment – taxi, climb (time, fuel and distance to the cruise level), cruise (TAS and fuel flow at that level, maximum cruise or best range), descent, alternate, holding and reserves – from the type's POH profile (C208: Figures 5-18, 5-19 and 5-25; GA8: AFM 5.3 climb rates and 5.8 cruise). Every figure can be amended; Recalculate from POH restores them, and Use this plan's EET and flow carries the result into the briefing and flight plan.

Winds: enter a wind per leg or Load winds (NAIPS) to fetch the wind and temperature profile for the route through the connector; the wind nearest the cruise level is applied to each leg and the ground speeds, leg times and trip fuel follow.

Personal NAIPS login: under Status › Operator link you can enter your own NAIPS username and password; briefings, winds and flight plan filing then use your account rather than the operator's. The login stays on the device and is sent to the connector with each request. Test NAIPS login confirms it.

The connector now reports what it provides; From roster and the fleet pack only appear when the operator actually has a roster feed, so a pilot or a small operator can use briefings, winds, filing and records without one.

Full app file for an EFB: Status › EFB files › Full app file builds a single HTML file of the whole app for this aircraft – W&B, performance, planning, records – on the device, for OzRunways or AvPlan documents. It keeps its own data on that device and does not update itself; rebuild it after an app update.

title: Flight sequence: pre-flight sign-off, enroute, completion and logbook
notes: The Plan tab now runs the flight in sequence with a step bar: Plan & brief → W&B → Perf → Pre-flight sign-off → Enroute → Complete → Logbook. Each step shows its status and jumps to the right page.

The record is accepted twice. The pre-flight acceptance covers the manifest, weight and balance, performance and plan and is signed before departure, when times are not yet known; the completion acceptance covers the times, landings, approach, fuel and fuel checks added after the flight. Each has its own fingerprint and both print on the record.

Times, landings, approach and fuel have moved from the manifest to the Enroute and Complete pages; each time field has a Now button and a clear (✕) button, and Clear times resets the whole block. Clear manifest and Clear loads and manifest now also clear the times.

Aerodrome search: find any of 2,680 Australian aerodromes by code, name or town and set it as departure, destination, alternate or a waypoint; legs are computed with great-circle track and distance, ETE from the TAS (nil wind), with Use computed EET; a route diagram works offline and Show map draws it on OpenStreetMap when online.

Enroute page: airborne time, ETA and SARTIME, the legs with planned fuel per leg, and fuel checks that compare fuel now with the plan, show the actual burn rate and project the fuel at destination against the fixed reserve.

Complete page: Complete flight copies the times onto the record and deducts the block time from the maintenance release; after the completion acceptance the logbook exports (LogTen, ForeFlight, CSV) are right there, then Start next flight clears the flight for the next sector.
Briefing option Include charts fetches NAIPS graphics (area forecast and wind/temperature charts) with the briefing when the connector supports it.

title: Plan tab: NAIPS briefing, requirements, fuel plan and flight plan filing
notes: New Plan tab. Enter the route, ETD, times, level and fuel policy; Get NAIPS briefing fetches the TAF, METAR/SPECI, TTF, NOTAM and SIGMET products for departure, destination and alternates through the operator connector, applies the alternate, holding, crosswind and NOTAM rules with every finding quoting the product it rests on, and works out the fuel required against the fuel on board in the W&B tab.
An optional plain-English summary (written by Claude on the connector, from the quoted products only) sits beside the raw products, labelled as a draft.

Flight plan: the ICAO fields are filled from the aircraft, the registration in W&B, the manifest and your pilot details; Preview shows the FPL text and File with NAIPS lodges it through the connector's NAIPS account. The briefing and the filed plan are attached to the next flight record.

The connector itself (connector/ in the repository) is the reference implementation: NAIPS SOAP client built from the published schema, decoder, rules engine, fuel planner and record store, with tests against a mock NAIPS. It needs a NAIPS account and Airservices' agreement for third-party use.

title: LogTen import fix
notes: LogTen entries now carry the out, off, on and in times as exact instants and the flight time as hours:minutes, so the in time and total time import even when LogTen does not know the aerodrome. The aircraft type is sent too, so a new registration is created as the right type instead of LogTen's default.

title: Take-offs and approach type on the flight record
notes: The times block now records take-offs and night take-offs alongside landings, and the approach flown: visual, or ILS, LOC, RNAV/RNP, VOR or NDB, classed as an instrument approach. All of them go onto the record, the CSV exports, the LogTen entry (day and night take-offs, approach) and the ForeFlight file.

title: Operator tools: logbook, roster, records upload, duty, currency, maintenance release
notes: C208B is now shown as C208.

Manifest: off-blocks, take-off, landing and on-blocks times with Now buttons (flight and air time worked out), landings, fuel uplift and fuel at shutdown, and per-passenger dangerous-goods declaration and safety-briefing acknowledgement, all carried on the flight record.
Logbook: each record can be sent straight to LogTen (its URL scheme), exported in ForeFlight's template layout or as a generic logbook CSV; the records list exports the whole logbook the same ways.

Operator link (Status › Operator link): connect to an operator's connector server to upload signed flight records automatically (queued until there is signal), load today's roster into the manifest with From roster, receive a fleet pack of registrations, customisations, standard weights and duty limit, and read company notices with read receipts. The connector interface is documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md.
Standard passenger weights: when the operator sets them, a Std button beside each passenger fills the approved weight and the record marks it.
Duty: Start duty / End duty on the Status page; the W&B page shows time on duty against the operator's limit.

Pilot currency: medical, flight review, IPC, line check, DG and emergency training dates with expiry warnings, plus hours and landings in the last 30/90/365 days counted from the records on the device.
Maintenance release: each registration can carry hours remaining and an expiry date; saving a flight record deducts its block time and the W&B page warns when hours or date are close.

title: C208B weight and balance and performance from the POH
notes: C208B Grand Caravan (G1000) performance from POH 208BPHBUS-00: the short field take-off and landing distance tables for both configurations, cargo pod installed and without pod, with the POH's wind, dry-grass and hot-day corrections, the lift-off and 50 ft speeds, the 10 kt tailwind limit, the ISA + 35 °C operating temperature limit and the 20 kt demonstrated crosswind. A Configuration selector on the Perf page chooses the charts.

C208B weight and balance template rewritten from POH Section 6: pilot and commuter seat arms, the six cabin cargo zones and four pod zones with their centroids and limits, fuel arm from the sample loading problem, maximum weights and the CG envelope read from the Figure 6-17 chart. VH-SMP, the POH sample loading problem airplane, is seeded as a deletable test registration and reproduces the POH's 8,750 lb take-off at 199.2 in.
Load AFM example on the C208B take-off page fills the POH sample (8,750 lb, 4,000 ft, 20 °C, 12 kt headwind: POH 2,933 ft / 1,669 ft).
Fix: a type's first surface is now treated as the paved baseline whatever it is called; the tabulated-data engine applies the hot-day rule and operating temperature limit.

title: Groundwork for tabulated POH performance data
notes: No visible change. The performance engine can now read POH performance tables (ground roll and total distance by weight, pressure altitude and temperature with percentage wind and surface corrections), as used by the Cessna 208 POH, ready for that data to be entered from the manual.

title: Digital sign-off of flight records
notes: Each saved flight record now has a Sign-off box: the pilot in command enters their name and optional licence number, ticks the acceptance statement and taps Accept and sign. The name, time and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the record are stored with it.

Opening a signed record recomputes the fingerprint and confirms the record is unchanged since sign-off. The sign-off and fingerprint are printed on the PDF, shown on the printout and included in the CSV log.
Signed records are marked in the Flight records list and need the usual two taps to delete.

title: Manifest and flight records
notes: Flight manifest on the W&B page: flight details, crew and passengers with seats and weights, baggage and freight with locations. The manifest fills the station loads automatically (switchable), so the W&B follows the manifest.

Save flight record keeps a dated snapshot of the manifest, the full weight and balance (every weight, arm and moment, the four conditions against their limits and the verdict) and the Perf tab's take-off and landing inputs and results. Records are listed in the W&B side panel.

Each record can be shared as a PDF built on the device (works offline), printed, copied as text or deleted, and carries a pilot-in-command signature line. Export log (CSV) gives one line per flight for a spreadsheet; Export records (JSON) exports everything.
Clear loads also clears the manifest when it is in use.

title: Performance tab: take-off and landing distances
notes: New Perf tab. Enter the aerodrome elevation, QNH, temperature, runway heading and the wind as broadcast on ATIS, AWIS or a METAR, the slope, surface and weight (or take the weight from the W&B tab) and the app reads the POH chart for you: pressure height, head and crosswind components, the take-off safety speed or reference approach speed for that weight, the distance to or from 50 ft and the ground roll, unfactored and with your safety factor, plus a sufficient / insufficient verdict against the runway length you enter.

GA8 charts from GA-FM-04 Section 5: take-off 14° flap, 3° powered-approach landing and power-off landing (with its rate of descent), digitised from the manual's drawing and followed exactly as on paper. The AFM's limits are enforced: no extrapolation above the chart, the lowest scheduled figure below it, 5 kt tailwind to 20 kt headwind, slopes to 2 %, 15 kt demonstrated crosswind warning.

A Load AFM example button fills each chart's worked example so the result can be compared with the manual. The take-off and power-off examples agree within 2 %; the 3° approach chart's printed example is about 10 % shorter than its own guide lines, which the app follows (the conservative reading) – see the note on that page.
Other types show the tab with a note that their charts have not been entered yet. All performance figures are marked unverified until checked against the POH.

title: GA8 weight and balance from the AFM
notes: GA8 W&B template now carries the station arms, fuel arm, cargo-zone limits and CG envelope from the GA8 manual GA-FM-04 (Section 2 limits and Section 6 trim sheets), in kilograms and millimetres from the firewall datum. Seat rows and freighter cargo zones are both listed.

An example GA8 registration, VH-WSM, is seeded once so the tab can be tried straight away. Its empty weight and arm are fictitious (the AFM worked example) and it is marked TEST DATA; delete it from Edit profile when you no longer need it and it stays deleted.
The template figures were transcribed by hand and remain marked unverified: confirm them against the AFM and the aircraft's own weight and balance report.

title: Weight and balance for the C208B and GA8
notes: New W&B tab: set up each registration with its empty weight and arm from the aircraft's weight and balance report, enter loads and fuel, and see zero-fuel, ramp, take-off and landing weights, CG arms, an in-or-out verdict and the envelope plot.
Type templates for the C208B (stations, limits, envelope – unverified, check against the POH) and the GA8 (layout and limits; arms and envelope entered from the AFM).
Registrations and last-used loads are kept on the device and travel with Export / Import.

title: Offline voice recognition (experimental)
notes: Status → Voice → Offline recognition: a one-off 46 MB download lets the app recognise replies, Say procedure and the “hey Aero” wake word on the device with no signal. It only listens for the words the app expects, which also makes it more accurate in engine noise.
The download is kept separately from the app and survives updates; Remove the offline download frees the space.
On Apple devices the microphone is released while the app speaks (switchable) so speech is never muted.
Smoother reading: the speech watchdog no longer restarts an utterance that has already begun, and the pause between challenge and response is a clean sentence break.

Wake-word commands wait for the whole phrase: a phrase the engine cuts short at a pause (“hey Aero, before … start checklist”) is joined with what follows, while an exact checklist name opens at once.
Smoother reading: the audio engine is no longer rebuilt around every line, cue tones release the audio hardware when idle, and the speech engine is only nudged when paused.
Offline engine: the microphone now stays open between lines by default, so replies are heard straight away and the switching click is gone; the accept tone is a soft short tick.
The checklist list no longer hides its last entries behind the voice bar, and it keeps its scroll position when the app refreshes.
Reset returns a checklist to the top; after each tick the checklist scrolls so the next item and those after it stay in view; a newly opened checklist always starts at the top.

title: Editable normal checklists
notes: Every normal checklist can be customised per aircraft: open it and tap Edit to add, change, remove or reorder lines, add notes, or restore the original. Edited checklists show ✎ in the list and “Customised on this device” under the title.
Export / Import on the Status page turns a device's customisations into text an operator can send to pilots, who paste it in.
Abnormal and emergency procedures are not editable.

Charts tab: one-tap links to the Airservices DAP, ERSA and NAIPS pages and to FD Pro, OzRunways or AvPlan if installed, with an aerodrome code for AIP searches. Charts cannot be embedded in the app; use iPad Split View alongside it.
Status → Customised checklists has a switch to use one approach checklist for every favourite (★) aircraft.
User guide brought fully up to date.
Charts tab: DAP and ERSA links now follow Airservices' dated amendment cycle, with the AIP index as a fallback; the Jeppesen button uses the FliteDeck Pro X link name.
Header tabs stay readable in iPad Split View. The Charts tab opens the NAIPS app directly, with the website beside it, and explains where ERSA lives.

title: “Hey Aero” wake word and a custom approach checklist
notes: Wake word (Status → Voice, off by default): with the app on screen, say “hey Aero, landing checklist”, “hey Aero, engine failure in flight”, “hey Aero, status” or “hey Aero, stop”. A red dot by the aircraft name shows it is listening. Uses battery and needs signal on Apple devices.

Custom approach checklist: create or edit your own approach checklist per aircraft from the Status page. It sits under Normal between Descent and Before Landing, is kept on this device, is read aloud like any other and opens with “hey Aero, approach checklist”.
Say procedure and the wake word understand plain names: landing, takeoff, start, shutdown, cruise, descent, taxi, climb, approach, and any procedure title.
Status → Voice shows the wake listener's state and the last words it heard, and more mis-hearings of “Aero” (euro, zero, hero, arrow…) are accepted.
Checklists opened by voice are now read aloud (the speech engine is primed by your first tap) and start by naming the checklist. Saying the wake word on its own can no longer tick a line.
Wake-word commands wait until you have finished speaking and prefer the checklist whose full name you said. Speech after a voice command is more reliable on Apple devices.
A spoken request to open a checklist always reads it, even if Read aloud was off. Status → Voice has a voice log for troubleshooting.
Apple devices: listening now always stops before the app speaks, so voice-opened checklists are read; the listening tone sounds when the microphone is actually live.
Voice commands recognise Before Start, Descent and After Landing correctly (an exact checklist name now wins over shortcuts).
Spoken checklist names tolerate mis-hearings a letter or two off (for example “dessert” for Descent).

title: Voice: read aloud, spoken replies and recall
notes: Read aloud (Status → Voice): the app speaks each line of an open checklist, waits for ✓ Checked, then reads the next. Works offline and in Bluetooth headsets. Speaking rate and voice are selectable.

Voice replies (experimental): after each line the app listens for “checked”, “set”, “repeat”, “skip” or “stop”. What it heard is shown before anything is applied. Needs microphone permission and, on Apple devices, signal.
Say procedure: with voice replies on, a microphone button above each checklist list lets you say a procedure name, for example “engine failure in flight”, and the app opens it.
All of this is off by default; nothing changes unless you turn it on.
Status → Voice has a Test the microphone button that reports exactly what the device says, and the voice bar names the reason when listening fails.
Spoken replies are acted on as soon as the word is heard, without waiting for the end-of-speech pause.
Default speaking rate lowered, with five steps from Slow to Fast; tapping a step plays a sample.
Normal checklists are read in short form: the challenge and the capitalised action only, with bracketed detail left on screen. Can be turned off under Status → Voice.

Listening is more dependable: the microphone stays open for as long as a line is waiting, opens a fraction of a second after the voice finishes, and accepts more ways of saying checked. Cue tones (one when listening, two when accepted) can be turned off.
Confirm a line by saying “checked” or the written response itself, for example “both on” or “idle cutoff”. Other words no longer tick a line.
The microphone now opens while the line is being read, so a reply is caught the moment the voice stops; anything heard before that is ignored. Switchable under Status → Voice.

title: Send to EFB, and Mac window fix
notes: The EFB rows on each Status page are now Send to EFB buttons: they open the share sheet with the file attached, so Copy to OzRWY or Save to Files is one tap. On a computer the file opens in the browser to save from there.
EFB files show a banner saying what they are, with a Share this file button and a link back to the app, so they are not mistaken for the app's own checklist.
On Mac and iPad installs the header now clears the window's close, minimise and zoom buttons.
If an EFB file is requested with no signal, a short message appears instead of the app page.
Version is shown as a plain number (1.7) in the app and in the EFB files; the build code moves to small print.

title: User guide
notes: A user guide explaining installation, the picker and favourites, working through checklists, emergency procedures, the Status page, day and night display, updates, offline use, EFB files and troubleshooting. Linked from the picker and every aircraft's Status page, and available offline.
Fixed: opening the app with signal now reliably loads the newest page on the first launch (a fault in the page fetch meant it could take one extra launch).

title: EFB files inside the app, and release notes
notes: Each aircraft's Status page now has an EFB files section: an interactive single-file checklist and a printable PDF for loading into OzRunways or AvPlan, with instructions.
The update bars now say what changed, with a What's new button. The Status page has a What's new row.
Hot and flooded start branches added to the Maule M-6 and M-7 engine start.

title: 30 aircraft and faster updates
notes: Added GA8 Airvan, Maule M-6-235 and M-7-235, King Air B200, Conquest II, Cessna 310R, 402C, 210M and 210R, Navajo, Chieftain, Malibu, Matrix and PC-12/45.
Opening the app with signal now always fetches the newest build instead of a cached copy.
Update bars are coloured: amber when a new version is waiting, green once applied.

title: Favourites and update awareness
notes: Star an aircraft to pin it under Favourites; the app offers this after three opens.
A bar announces a downloaded update while the app is open and an applied update on the next launch; the Status page shows the version and a manual check.

title: Day and night modes, cockpit colours
notes: Header switch cycles Auto, Day and Night; remembered on the device.
Normal, Abnormal and Emergency tabs coloured green, amber and red; warnings red, cautions amber; next-item marker takes the tab colour.

title: Multi-aircraft app
notes: Aircraft picker with 16 common GA types, progress kept per aircraft, V-speeds page and deep links by aircraft id.

title: C208B offline checklist
notes: First installable version with the Cessna 208B checklists, saved progress and offline use.
